This is a general exclusion from the Regulation, so it applies automatically.
The Commission's clarification note 3 from 2007 is older and out of date: it described a 50 km limit and an exemption that each Member State could choose whether to grant.

Member States may still have national rules for vehicles outside the EU Regulation's scope.

On an occasional passenger service, the 45-minute break due after 4.5 hours of driving can be replaced by two breaks of at least 15 minutes each.
They must be spread over the 4.5-hour driving period so that you still meet the basic rule.
Normally the split allowed is at least 15 minutes followed by at least 30 minutes.
Separately, the working time rules still apply.
You must not work more than six hours in a row without a break.
Your breaks must total at least 30 minutes if your working time is 6 to 9 hours, and at least 45 minutes if it is over 9 hours.
Those breaks can be split into periods of at least 15 minutes.
